title: Wise Words
subtitle: WITH MARCO REYES  ·  STORY NIGHT

segments.head: TONIGHT: PATRICE DRIVES
segments.author: Wise Words
lines: Good evening, everyone.
I'm Marco Reyes, and this is Wise Words.
Tonight's story is about Patrice Gagnon, a hospital cafeteria cook from Lewiston, Maine.
She is fifty-one. She can feed four hundred people before lunch.
But she had never driven a car. Not once.

segments.head: CHAPTER 1: NO MORE BUS
segments.quote: Even if you are on the right track you will get run over if you just sit there.
segments.author: Tom Sims
lines: Her ex always drove. Then the city cut her bus route.
So she walked two miles to work in the sleet, grumbling.
Her coworker Gail taped a note to the soup pot, from the humorist Tom Sims:
Even if you are on the right track you will get run over if you just sit there.
That Friday, Patrice got her learner's permit at the BMV. Her photo looks like a hostage.

segments.head: CHAPTER 2: THE DRIVER'S SEAT
segments.quote: Courage is not the absence of fear, but rather the judgment that something else is more important than fear.
segments.author: Ambrose Redmoon
lines: Her nephew Kevin tossed her the keys to his old Honda.
In the church parking lot, her hands shook on the wheel.
Kevin read her a line from the writer Ambrose Redmoon:
Courage is not the absence of fear, but rather the judgment that something else is more important than fear.
Her paycheck was more important. Her freedom, too. She turned the key.

segments.head: CHAPTER 3: THE HORN
segments.quote: To avoid unkind criticism: say nothing, be nothing, do nothing.
segments.author: Elbert Hubbard
lines: Out on Lisbon Street, she drove fifteen miles an hour. A pickup honked. Then a minivan.
She wanted to cry into the glove box.
Then she remembered Elbert Hubbard, an old American writer:
To avoid unkind criticism: say nothing, be nothing, do nothing.
She waved, smiled, and kept going. Twenty-five miles an hour. Wild.

segments.head: CHAPTER 4: THE CONES
segments.quote: We are what we repeatedly do. Excellence, then, is not an act but a habit.
segments.author: Will Durant
lines: In March, at her road test, she knocked over every cone in parallel parking.
The examiner said, well, you're thorough.
At home, Kevin showed her a line from the historian Will Durant:
We are what we repeatedly do. Excellence, then, is not an act but a habit.
Every night after work, she parked between two trash cans. Her neighbor brought a lawn chair.

segments.head: CHAPTER 5: THE OPEN ROAD
segments.quote: Our battered suitcases were piled on the sidewalk again; we had longer ways to go. But no matter, the road is life.
segments.author: Jack Kerouac
lines: In May, she passed. She bought a used Subaru with a dent shaped like Ohio.
Still, she only drove to work and back.
Gail lent her an old copy of Jack Kerouac's On the Road, with one line underlined:
Our battered suitcases were piled on the sidewalk again; we had longer ways to go. But no matter, the road is life.
Saturday morning, Patrice packed a cooler and picked up Gail.

segments.head: CHAPTER 6: SALT WATER
segments.quote: I know of a cure for everything: salt water.
segments.author: Isak Dinesen
lines: They drove to Popham Beach. Patrice merged onto the highway and only screamed a little.
Ankle-deep in the cold Atlantic, Gail quoted Isak Dinesen, a Danish writer:
I know of a cure for everything: salt water.
Sweat from the trash cans. Tears from the cones. And now, the sea.
Patrice laughed and got her socks wet.

segments.head: THAT'S TONIGHT'S STORY
segments.quote: Get moving. Be brave. Ignore the horns. Practice. Take the road. Find the sea.
segments.author: Marco Reyes
lines: That's tonight's story.
Get moving. Be brave. Ignore the honking. Practice. Take the long road. Find the sea.
I drive like Patrice, by the way. The honking is my fans saying hello.
I'm Marco Reyes. Good night.
